description: 301 redirect rules for Apache, Nginx, HTML and JavaScript.

faqs.a: Apache .htaccess uses Redirect 301, Nginx uses rewrite … permanent, HTML uses a meta refresh tag, and JavaScript uses window.location.replace — all four are generated from the same list.
A 301 tells browsers and search engines the move is permanent, so link equity passes to the new URL. Meta refresh and JavaScript redirects are client-side fallbacks.
faqs.q: Is a 301 better than a meta refresh?

faqs.a: Yes — old paths are regex-escaped for Nginx and quotes are escaped for Apache, HTML and JavaScript output.

howto: Enter one redirect per line as: old-path -> new-url.
Switch between the Apache, Nginx, HTML and JavaScript tabs.
Copy the block you need into your server config or page.
